transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess I came in because I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like, at work, I'm a business operations specialist, and I just feel like I'm a terrible employee. And a bad homeowner, too. I just feel like I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. Actually, speaking of my house, the gutters have been overflowing every time it rains. It's making this huge puddle right by the front steps, and my neighbor's cat keeps coming over to drink from it. It's an orange tabby, really friendly, but I'm worried it's going to get sick from the dirty water. I tried calling a guy to fix the gutters, but he never called me back, which just proves I can't even handle basic house maintenance. It's just all my fault.
Have you been feeling this way most of the time for at least the past two years, or is this a more recent change?

Um, yeah, I guess it's been a while. Like, the depression and just... not caring about anything anymore, it's been with me for about two years and one month, I think. Speaking of months, last month was my sister's birthday, and I usually bake her a cake, you know? A chocolate one with raspberry filling, it's her favorite. But this year, I just... I couldn't even bring myself to go to the grocery store to get the ingredients. I just sat on the couch staring at the wall. And then I felt so guilty about it, which just makes me feel like an even worse sister. She said it was fine, but I know she was disappointed. She ended up just getting a store-bought cake from the bakery down the street, the one next to that old dry cleaner that closed down recently. I wonder what they're going to put in that space... maybe a coffee shop? But anyway, yeah, it's been over two years of feeling like this.

During these past two years, have there been any periods of several weeks or longer where your mood was significantly worse, to the point where you could barely function at all, compared to how you feel most of the time?

Looking back, honestly, the low mood and just... the total loss of interest in everything, it's been there for almost the whole time since this started. It's not really like it dips for a few weeks and comes back up, because there have only been really, really brief periods where I could function a little better. 

Like, I remember one of those brief times, I actually managed to leave the house and buy a plant. It was a Boston fern. They're supposed to be really good for indoor air quality, which I need because my apartment is right near a major bus stop. The buses idle there for like ten minutes at a time, and the exhaust is just awful. The city really needs to switch to electric buses, honestly. I was reading this report—well, not for work, I was procrastinating on a spreadsheet—about municipal transit budgets, and it's crazy how much they still spend on diesel. My friend Sarah takes the 42 bus every day, and she says it's always running late anyway. She works at the public library downtown, in the basement archives, which sounds so nice and quiet compared to the street noise. 

But um, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, it hasn't really gotten worse in specific chunks because it's just been a constant low, pretty much this entire time.

During these past two years, have you ever experienced a period of several days or longer where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or euphoric, to the point where your behavior was noticeably different from your usual self?

Um, energetic? No, not really. I mean, I can't even remember the last time I felt like I had energy to spare. I'm usually just so tired. Like, even just making coffee in the morning feels like running a marathon. I got this new coffee maker, actually, one of those pour-over ones with the reusable metal filter? It's supposed to be better for the environment because you aren't throwing away paper filters every day. I try to be eco-friendly where I can, you know? Like recycling my cardboard boxes. I get so many packages now because I just order everything online since I don't want to go to the store. The delivery guy, Mike, he's super nice. He always leaves the boxes right behind the planter so they don't get wet if it rains. He drives one of those electric delivery vans, which is great, going back to what I was saying about the buses. But yeah, no, I haven't had any days where I felt super energetic or talkative or anything like that. Just... tired.
Aside from feeling tired and lacking energy, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or how much you are eating?

Um, yeah, my appetite has been... it's kind of all over the place, honestly. But mostly, I just skip real meals during the day. Like, I'll be working, or well, trying to work, and I just can't be bothered to make anything. I've basically been living on coffee, toast, and whatever is easiest to grab without cooking. I actually bought this really nice sourdough from the bakery I mentioned earlier, the one by the old dry cleaner? Sourdough is supposed to be better for your gut health, I read an article about the microbiome and how it affects your mood. The gut-brain axis, they call it. It's fascinating how much bacteria we have in our stomachs, like trillions of them. My friend Sarah, the one at the library, she started making her own kombucha because of that. She has this big glass jar on her counter with a SCOBY in it—it looks like a weird alien pancake, to be honest. I don't think I could stomach drinking something that came from that, but she swears by it. She even flavors it with ginger and lemon. 

But um, anyway, yeah, I've noticed my clothes are definitely looser lately. I guess I'm just not eating enough actual food, just the toast and stuff.
How has your sleep been during these past two years?

Um, my sleep? It's been pretty awful, honestly. Most nights I just lie awake for hours in the dark, just listening to the house settle. It makes these really distinct creaking noises. It's an older building, built in the 1920s, I think. They used real hardwood floors back then, not like that cheap gray laminate they put in all the new apartments downtown. My sister just moved into one of those new high-rises, and she says it looks nice but the soundproofing is terrible. She can hear her neighbor's TV every single night. He watches a lot of reality shows, apparently. I don't really get the appeal of reality TV, to be honest, it's all so obviously scripted. Like, you know the producers are just setting up situations to create drama for the ratings. 

Though I did try watching that British baking show once, which is actually really soothing. The big white tent they film in is so pretty, out in the countryside. I always wonder what happens to all the leftover cake and bread they bake on that show. Like, do the camera crews eat it? It seems like a huge waste if they just throw it away. Food waste is such a massive issue, especially in the restaurant industry. I was looking at some supply chain data for work—I do operations, so I look at a lot of efficiency metrics—and the amount of inventory spoilage is just crazy. 

But, wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, sleeping. Yeah. So I lie awake listening to the house creak, and then even when I finally do drift off, I always wake up around three or four in the morning. And then that's just it. I just stare at the ceiling and can't get back to sleep at all before I have to log on for work.
You mentioned feeling like everything is your fault; do you often feel an intense sense of worthlessness or guilt that seems out of proportion to the situation?

Um, yeah, I do. That's actually a big part of why I came in. I just... I can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is entirely my fault. Like I'm just a terrible employee, and a bad homeowner, and I just deserve to lose everything I've worked for. It's this heavy, awful feeling. 

Speaking of being a homeowner, my gutters are completely clogged right now. I noticed it when it rained last week, the water was just pouring over the sides like a waterfall. I really need to get up there and clean them out, or hire someone to do it. But hiring people is so expensive these days. I had a plumber come out last month to fix a leaky faucet in the guest bathroom, and he charged me like two hundred dollars just for the service call. He was a nice guy, though, he had this really cute golden retriever puppy in his truck. He showed me a picture of it sleeping in a laundry basket. Golden retrievers are so sweet, they just love everyone. I thought about getting a dog once, maybe a rescue from the shelter. They have so many older dogs that need good homes. Puppies are a lot of work, you have to potty train them and they chew on everything. My cousin got a lab puppy and it chewed right through the leg of her antique dining table. It was this beautiful mahogany table that belonged to our grandmother. Mahogany is such a gorgeous wood, they don't really make furniture like that anymore, do they? It's all that cheap particle board stuff you have to assemble yourself with an Allen wrench. I hate assembling furniture, I always end up with a screw leftover and I have no idea where it was supposed to go. 

But um, yeah, the guilt. It's just always there. Like I'm just fundamentally doing everything wrong.

Because you have been feeling so overwhelmed by this sense of guilt and worthlessness, have you ever reached a point where you felt like you didn't want to be here anymore, or that you would be better off dead?

Um, no, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I feel awful, and the guilt is just exhausting, but I don't want to die or anything like that. I just want the feeling to stop. 

It is really exhausting, though. Being tired all the time makes everything harder, even just driving to the grocery store. I try to go early on Sunday mornings when it's not so crowded. The parking lot at my local store is a nightmare on weekend afternoons. It's one of those lots where the lanes are too narrow, and people are always backing out without looking. I saw a fender bender there just a couple of weeks ago. This lady in a silver SUV backed right into a little red sedan. The sound was awful, that crunching metal sound. It reminded me of when I was in high school and I accidentally backed my dad's car into the mailbox. Our mailbox was made of brick, so it completely smashed the bumper. My dad was so mad. He had just washed the car, too. He used to spend hours on Saturday mornings washing and waxing his car. He had all these special microfiber towels and different kinds of wax for different parts of the car. It seemed like a lot of work just for something that's going to get dirty the next time it rains. Rain always leaves those little water spots, especially if you park under a tree. There's this big oak tree near my driveway, and it drops acorns everywhere in the fall. The squirrels love it, though. They bury them all over my yard. I keep finding little holes in the grass where they've been digging. 

But, um, no. To answer your question, I haven't had any thoughts about wanting to be dead. Just... wishing I could do things right, I guess.
Do you find it difficult to focus on your work or make simple decisions during the day?

Um, yeah, I guess so. I don't really know. It's just hard to, like, sit down and get through the spreadsheets I need to look at. I'll just stare at the screen. My monitor is actually getting this weird flicker in the corner. I think it's the HDMI cable, honestly. The IT guy at work—his name is Kevin, he's always wearing these really loud Hawaiian shirts—he told me that those cables go bad all the time if you bend them too much. I try not to bend it, but my desk is pushed right up against the wall, so it kind of squishes the cords in the back. I got the desk from Ikea a few years ago. It's one of those standing desks, but I never actually use the standing feature. The motor makes this loud humming noise when it goes up, and it always startles my cat. She's a rescue, a little tabby, and she's super skittish. She hides under the sofa whenever anyone comes over. The sofa has this huge rip underneath it now because she uses it like a hammock. I should probably get it fixed, or just buy a new one, but furniture shopping is so overwhelming. There are just too many choices, you know? Like, do you want velvet or linen? And then what color? 

But um, what were you asking? Oh, focusing. Yeah, I just... I don't really know if I have trouble making decisions or focusing, it's just all kind of a blur right now.
